bracket: [Textbook misprint: the printed solution states that Al, Si and P 'belong to 13 period in the periodic table'. They are period-3 elements, belonging to groups 13, 14 and 15 respectively. The reasoning that follows — that they share the same valence shell, so the rising nuclear charge holds the valence electrons more tightly — is correct and does not depend on the slip. The solution is preserved as printed.]

[Textbook misprint: the question as printed asks why \(\mathrm{Ga^{3\oplus}}\) salts are the better reducing agent. \(\mathrm{Ga^{3\oplus}}\) is gallium in its highest and, for a light group 13 element, most stable oxidation state; it cannot be oxidised further and so cannot act as a reducing agent. On the chapter's own inert-pair reasoning the reducing species is gallium in the \(+1\) state, which is readily oxidised to the stable \(+3\) state. The stem is transcribed as printed and the contrast the question is drawing is answered above.]
